sources: New York Times investigation (former Polar LNG CEO Joel Riddle + two other sources + messages reviewed by the NYT + Baker Botts legal memos); corroborated by Financial Times and Wall Street Journal

sections.what_happened: Sanctioned Russian LNG producer Novatek secretly provided seed funding to US startup Polar LNG, which plans to liquefy Alaska North Slope gas for export to Asia using a ~640,000-ton Novatek gravity-based offshore liquefaction structure, and is seeking a minority stake. Funding was routed via Abu Dhabi-based Tech Wave Industrial Projects Management (whose senior executives are former Novatek staff); messages reviewed by the NYT discuss up to $15 million for Tech Wave to support Polar LNG, including an expected first transfer of $5 million. Former CEO Joel Riddle resigned in September after learning the funding's true origin (he had been told it came from a UAE firm; he also says claimed investor Gentry Beach never invested); CFO Dan Chandra and other executives also left. Baker Botts legal memos attached to Riddle's resignation said Treasury's sanctions-enforcement office had raised potential Russia-related sanctions concerns. Witkoff and Kushner discussed the technology proposal with Putin during their September visit; it is unclear whether they knew of the financing. Polar LNG says Riddle was terminated for cause, its work complies with US law, and it is investigating his claims. Novatek, the White House, Treasury and State did not comment to the NYT/WSJ.
sections.what_verified: Three independent T2 publisher families: New York Times (originating investigation), Financial Times, Wall Street Journal (Oct 25 follow-up confirming executive departures and the funding allegation). Kyiv Independent and Alaska News carry the same NYT/FT reporting and add no independent family.
sections.what_disputed: Polar LNG's rebuttal: Riddle was 'terminated for cause' (company says his resignation letter predated a termination letter by six days), the company calls him a disgruntled former employee, says its work complies with US law and that it is investigating his claims. No US agency has confirmed a sanctions violation; the Treasury concern is reported via legal memos, not an OFAC finding. Polar LNG is NOT the state-partnered Alaska LNG project (Glenfarne/Alaska Gasline) -- conflating them would be an error.
sections.why_matters: While Washington negotiates peace with Moscow, sanctioned Russian gas money was secretly funding an Alaska LNG startup -- and the US executives quit over it.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (NYT Oct 23 investigation, in no Oct 24 or Oct 25 scan) -- Sanctioned Russian gas giant Novatek secretly funded US startup Polar LNG's Alaska project; deal discussed by Witkoff/Kushner with Putin in September
